questions: Did the difficulty walking begin suddenly, within minutes or hours?
Did it begin after a fall or other injury?
Do you have pain in either leg or hip when standing or walking?
Do you feel that one side of your body is weaker than the other?
Do you have numbness or tingling in your legs?
Have you had facial drooping, speech difficulty, or weakness of an arm?
Do you feel dizzy or as though the room is spinning when you stand?
Have you lost consciousness or had a seizure during one of these episodes?
Do your legs tremble or give way despite being able to move them normally while seated or lying down?
Have you had similar episodes before?
Have you ever been diagnosed with a stroke?
Did the facial drooping or arm weakness begin at the same time as your walking difficulty?
Are the facial drooping and arm weakness still present now?
Is the facial drooping or arm weakness on the same side as the leg difficulty?
Have you been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, Parkinson’s disease, or another neurological disorder?
Do you have diabetes, high blood pressure, or atrial fibrillation?
Have you previously been able to walk independently without a wheelchair or another person’s help?
Does your walking improve when you are distracted or when nobody is physically helping you?
orders: Bedside neurological examination including cranial nerves, muscle strength, tone, reflexes, sensation, coordination, and plantar responses.
Hoover sign testing during attempted hip extension.
Observe gait and sit-to-stand transfer with and without distraction, including tandem walking if safe.
Test for a positive hip-abduction sign and inconsistency of leg weakness between formal testing and functional movement.
MRI brain without contrast, including sagittal T1-weighted imaging, to assess for midbrain atrophy (“hummingbird sign”) and exclude structural lesions.
Levodopa therapeutic trial with carbidopa–levodopa, titrated to escalated tolerated dose for at least 4 weeks, assessing gait, rigidity, and bradykinesia response.
served: deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses
gait observation including turning and doorways
MRI brain - midbrain (hummingbird sign, midbrain-to-pons ratio)
